entry.title: ENABLE RELIGION FIELD IN INFOTYPE 0002
entry.content:
Introduction:

The Religion field, known as KONFE exists in the Infotype 0002 structure and is kept in the PA0002 table. Yet the Religion field does not show up on the Infotype 0002 screen. This document walks through each step to find the screen settings turn on the Religion field and set it up as a dropdown so that users can choose the needed religion from the list.

Requirement:

The Religion field is missing from Infotype 0002 even though it is present in the PA0002 table. We must activate the Religion field in Infotype 0002. Provide a dropdown for it.

Infotype 0002

Table: PA0002

Checking the status of the field in module pool:

1. First, we must find the program and screen number that belong to Infotype 0002. To do this go to PA30 enter the employee number select the infotype and click on the existing data record. On that screen choose System → Status.

In my case the program is MP000200, and the screen number is 2010.

2. To enable the Religion field in Infotype 0002 we need to modify the screen.

Change screen modifications:

SPRO → Personnel Management → Personnel Administration → Customizing User Interfaces → Change screen Modifications

Search for the module pool MP000200 and locate screen number 2010.

In the screenshot, no Religion field appears in the grouping. If the Religion field were present in the grouping, we could then control whether it is shown or hidden.

Solution:

1. If the grouping does not exist in the module pool use T-code PM01 to see whether the Religion field is part of the structure. If the Religion field is in the structure but missing from the module pool screen modifications we must add the Religion field to the screen painter layout.

2. Use T-code SE51, enter the program and screen number. Click the layout editor.

The screen modifications currently contain groupings up to 026. We will create a grouping, 027 for the Religion field. In this grouping we can set the line number, column number and group.

 

For the values we can also define a dropdown for the Religion field.

Output:

The Religion field now shows up in Infotype 0002, and users can select the value from a dropdown.

Conclusion:

The Religion field has been successfully activated in Infotype 0002. We verified the structure identified the right screen and module pool and added the KONFE field to the layout. The Religion field is now ready for users to maintain, complete with a dropdown, for choosing the religion. The selected value will be saved in the PA0002-KONFE.

entry.title: Leveraging Joule Studio for SAP SuccessFactors
entry.content:
I'm excited to share my first blog, based on my learnings and experience working with Joule Studio. @amrutha_g will be the co-author of this blog.

This blog introduces Joule Studio and demonstrates how SAP SuccessFactors users can create tailored conversational experiences using Actions, Skills, and Agents. Through a practical illustration, readers will learn how to build, test, and deploy AI-powered capabilities that enable users to extract business information by communication through natural language.

  1. Introduction to Joule Studio 
  2. Key Features of Joule Studio 
  3. Prerequisites  
  4. Understanding the Three Building Blocks of Joule Studio 
  5. Action Editor Overview 
  6. Skill Editor Deep Dive 
  7. Agent Editor Overview 
  8. Testing Skills and Agents 
  9. Conclusion

Introduction

Joule Studio is an important component of SAP Build; it's a comprehensive suite of low-code and no-code solutions designed to enhance application development and leverage the power of generative AI.

It let’s us expand Joule's capabilities and knowledge to meet the distinct requirements of the organization.

With Joule embedded in SAP SuccessFactors, Joule Studio serves as a workspace to create and deploy custom capabilities. These can in turn be used within our instance to perform informational/ transactional operations with the help of prompts in human language.

Features

  • Develop new skills for Joule that enable it to perform additional, custom, and pre-determined tasks that supports business processes.
  • Design interactive Joule agents that collaborate with Joule to tackle complex or multi-step tasks efficiently.
  • Manage and deploy advanced versions of skills and Joule agents to promote ongoing enhancements and flexibility.

Let us consider a scenario to understand more:

A user has an Employee ID. Using that, they want to fetch the first name and last name of the employee. Instead of navigating around the SuccessFactors UI and searching for an Employee, the user would like to simply ask Joule.

Prerequisites

  • An active user (developer) license is required to build, test, and deploy your custom Joule skills.
  • Joule should be enabled in the SuccessFactors instance

Building Blocks of Joule Studio

There are mainly 3 - building blocks of Joule Studio:

  1. Actions: An action is SAP's building block that wraps a single API call (or endpoint) - defining its inputs and outputs — so that it can be securely exposed and reused inside a Joule Skill or Agent.
  2. Skills: A skill is part of an advanced AI model and can act on specific operations by leveraging the content of the conversation. It helps in combining various Actions together
  3. Agents: A Joule agent is an independent, multipurpose-tool system that solves complex problems by selecting and executing appropriate tools dynamically. It helps combine various skills together.

Creating any of the above blocks requires a project. A project serves as a comprehensive workspace where we can create and manage various skills and agents related to a particular use case.

Before proceeding, start by creating a new project in Joule Studio.

Refer this Create a Project in Joule Studio, classic edition | SAP Help Portal to create a project.

Action Editor

The Action Editor is the workspace where we can create, modify, and manage actions.

The action editor makes API operations available to actions while also simplifying input and output values. We can also use the editor to test the operation of an action. To obtain reusable action artifacts, release and publish the Actions project to the library.

For this scenario, we would be using the Get Entities from User API

The image below illustrates the Action Editor.

The Actions pane consists of a complete list of all the API actions related to the project.

For each API, we have three tabs available: Input, Output and Test.

  • The Input tab is used to define the parameters required by the API to retrieve the desired data. These input parameters are passed to the API during execution and determine the results returned by the API.

Following are the fields available in the Input tab can be used to customize and refine the output returned by the API call.

  • $top: Specifies the maximum number of records to retrieve. By default, all available records are returned.
  • $skip: Specifies the number of records to skip before returning the results.
  • $count: Returns the total number of records that match the query criteria.
  • $filter: Applies conditions to filter the results based on specific field values.
  • $search: Searches for records that match the specified search value.
  • $orderby: Sorts the results based on one or more selected fields.

For our case, we have added the below condition to the $filter tab. ‘userId’ is the corresponding field for the employee ID.

To know more about the API’s and their fields definitions, you can refer to the SAP documentation below:
About SAP SuccessFactors APIs | SAP Help Portal

  • The Output tab consists of two sections: Header and Body. The Body section displays the fields which would be returned by the API call. Here, we can add or remove fields as needed to customize the output according to the requirements. For our scenario, we have retained the fields below and removed the rest.

  • The Test tab is used to validate and test the API using sample input values before using it into actual skill. It helps ensure that the API returns the expected results and allows us to refine the query parameters as needed. Provide the employee ID in $search field and try testing the API

For more information about the Action Editor, refer to below document from SAP:
Overview of an Action Editor | SAP Help Portal

Skill Editor

The Skill Editor is the workspace used to create, modify, and manage skills in Joule Studio.

Skills can be built using any of the following Activities:

  1. Action: Use one or more actions that have been created and incorporate them into the skill workflow.
  2. Process: Configure the skill to invoke a process created in SAP Build Process Automation.
  3. Automation: Configure the skill to trigger an automation built using SAP Build Process Automation.
  4. Skill: Reuse an existing Joule skill by incorporating it into another skill.
  5. Condition: Add decision-making logic to the skill by defining conditions that control the workflow based on specific criteria.

For more information about the activities, refer here: Add Activities to the Skill | SAP Help Portal

In the example shown below, a skill - EmployeeDetails has been created by incorporating an Action into the skill workflow.

The Trigger tab is where we define the basic details of a skill, including its Name, Identifier, and Description. The Identifier is automatically generated and pre-populated by the system.

The Description plays a significant role in aiding the Joule Assistant to understand the skill's purpose and area of specialization. This will allow Joule to identify and invoke the most relevant skill based on the user's prompt.

The Trigger tab is the place where we also define the input and output parameters for the skill.

  • Skill Inputs are variables that capture the information required from the end user. Ex: empid
  • Skill Outputs are used to store the data returned by the skill upon execution. In this case, we will define the variable of type list, so that it returns all the relevant fields.
    For our case, we will define the output of type list, so that it fetches all the relevant results returned by the API call.  

These parameters serve as the interface through which information is passed in and out of the skill.

Next, we can add an Action to the skill workflow by selecting the + icon. This is the action that was created in the previous step.

Each action consists of three tabs: General, Inputs, and Outputs.

The General tab displays the action name along with the Destination Variable. The destination variable stores the endpoint of the instance through which the information needs to be obtained. This will be created by us.

It allows the skill to access and map the action's output data to the appropriate fields, conditions, or downstream actions.

The Inputs tab is used to map the input variables defined earlier in the skill. These variables are passed to the action to ensure that the API receives the correct input values during execution.

In most cases, input variables are configured within the $filter parameter to retrieve the required data based on specific criteria.

Formulas can also be used to combine multiple input variables, aiding the creation of dynamic and more complex API queries.

In this case, the below expression has been used in the $filter tab. We have mapped userId field in the API definition to our skill Input - empid.

The Outputs tab displays the fields returned by the API call. It allows us to view the data that will be available after the action is executed and identify the output fields that can be used in subsequent steps of the skill workflow.

In the End section, map the skill's output variables to the appropriate fields returned by the action. This ensures that the relevant data retrieved from the API call is exposed as the final output of the skill and can be presented to the user or consumed by downstream processes. For this scenario, we have mapped the API result list to our output variable.

Agent Editor

Agents are created by combining one or more skills and providing detailed instructions that define how those skills should be aligned to perform a particular task.

By combining skills with proper execution logic, agents can interpret user requests, determine the relevant actions to be performed, and delivers the required outcome.

Refer to the below SAP documentation to know more about the Agent Editor

Create a Joule Agent | SAP Help Portal

For our case, we will add the 'EmployeeDetails' skill to the tool and provide instructions as below:

“When a user provides an Employee ID, invoke the EmployeeDetails skill using the supplied Employee ID as input. Retrieve the employee information from the skill response and present the results to the user in a clear and structured format. If the Employee ID is missing, prompt the user to provide it. If no employee record is found, inform the user accordingly.”

Testing the Skill/Agent

Once satisfied with the configuration of the skill or agent, select Test to validate its functionality. During testing, provide the appropriate connection details and endpoints for the SAP SuccessFactors instance to ensure successful execution and accurate results.

The image below shows the Joule Test tab.

The above image shows the testing of our skill.

Here, users can test the skill or agent by entering a prompt in natural, conversational language. Joule analyses the prompt and calls the most appropriate skill or agent to handle the request.

On entering the employee ID, Joule fetches the employee’s details from the instance.

Verify that the system correctly identifies and invokes the desired skill or agent based on the user's input. Once the execution is successful, the response is displayed in the chat interface in a clear and structured format, allowing us to validate both the behavior of the skill and the accuracy of the returned results.

After testing, deploy the project. This ensures that the Agent is ready to be used within the Joule chat in the instance.

Conclusion

The blog helps us to explore Joule Studio, and how it can be leveraged for SuccessFactors. It also explains how Actions, Skills, and Agents can contribute to building these experiences. An Action enables a specific operation, Skills help us combine actions, and Agents can help orchestrate these skills together.

With Joule Studio, the possibilities go beyond what the user can find in the application —they can also change how the user interacts with it.

entry.title: Enforcing Minimum Rest Period at Record Save in SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking
entry.content:
The EU Working Time Directive mandates a minimum 11-hour rest between two consecutive working periods. SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking supports Rest Rules that highlight violations on the timesheet and can block submission (KBA 3323455).

But both act at the timesheet level. The employee can save non-compliant entries all week - and only find out at submission.

What if we block it right when they hit Save?

The Idea

Two building blocks:

  1. A valuation step that writes each day’s actual clock-in/clock-out into a Time Container.
  2. A validation rule on the Time Recording Profile that reads adjacent days from that container on every save, calculates the rest gap, and raises a hard error if it falls below the threshold.
Fig. 1 - Solution Architecture Diagram

Building Block 1: The Time Container

We need the validation rule to know when the employee actually started and stopped working on adjacent days. A Time Container makes this possible.

Input Group

A time type group containing all attendance types that count as actual working time.

Fig. 2 - Attendance time type group and its members

Output Group

A time type group with Time Container Type = Yes. This is what the rule will query.

Fig. 3 - Output group with Time Container Type enabled

Valuation Step

Aggregate Input Groups and Split, Valuate Per Day, Threshold = 0. All attendance records are aggregated into the container, storing the earliest start and latest end per employee per day.

Fig. 4 - Aggregation valuation step

Building Block 2: The Validation Rule

A business rule assigned as a Validation Rule on the Time Recording Profile. It fires on every record save.

Variables

The rule uses Lookup(Time Container) to fetch the previous day’s end time and the next day’s start time. Current-day times come from the record being saved.

Fig. 5 - Variable definitions: Time Container lookups and date arithmetic

Backward Check - Previous Day

Did the employee rest enough between yesterday’s last clock-out and today’s clock-in?

The rule calculates the gap in seconds. If < 39,600 (11 hours) - error, save blocked.

An overnight detection is built in: if the previous day’s end time is numerically smaller than its start time, the shift crossed midnight, and the DateTime construction adjusts the calendar date accordingly.

Fig. 6 - Previous-day rest gap check with overnight handling

Forward Check - Next Day

If tomorrow is already recorded, does today’s clock-out leave enough rest before tomorrow’s clock-in?

Same logic, reversed direction. Same overnight handling.

Fig. 7 - Next-day rest gap check with overnight handling

The Error

“A minimum rest period of 11 hours is required between two working periods. Please review and adjust your time entries.”

Raised with Error severity - the record cannot be saved.

Quick Example

 MondayTuesday
Saved entry08:00 - 19:0004:00 - 12:00
Rest gap 19:00 → 04:00 = 9 hours
ResultSavedBlocked (< 11 hours)

Employee adjusts Tuesday to 06:00 - 12:00 (gap = 11h). Save succeeds.

At a Glance

 Standard Rest RulesThis Approach
Blocks atTimesheet submissionRecord save
FeedbackEnd of periodImmediate

The two are complementary - standard rest rules for visual indicators, this approach for hard enforcement at entry.

Worth Noting

  • The rule checks against already saved adjacent days. If the adjacent day has not been recorded yet, the lookup returns null and the check is skipped.
  • 39,600 seconds = 11 hours. Adjust to match your regulation.
  • Test overnight shifts thoroughly - they are the trickiest edge case.

entry.title: Say goodbye to cloning policy changed time recording profile! Effective-dated Time Valuation is here
entry.content:
Overview

Every HR admin who has ever managed time in a large, multi-country enterprise knows the complex challenges that comes with a single sentence in an email: "The collective bargaining agreement has been updated. Changes effective June 1."

What follows is a familiar scramble. You need to change an overtime threshold in your Time Recording Profile. But the profile is shared across thousands of employees. So, you clone it, rename it, update the threshold in the new clone, then mass-update Job Information records so employees are switched over on exactly the right date. Then someone asks: "What about the weekly timesheet that spans May 31 and June 1?" The Time Sheet is split and requires to be handled as part of payroll run.

I've heard this story from customers across industries — manufacturing in Germany, healthcare in Australia, retail in France. The pain is universal. The root cause? Time Valuations were not adapting to these changes themselves. A configuration object that calculates when people work, how much they earn, and whether rules are met — couldn't change over time without an admin/partner's intervention.

That's why we designed Effective-Dated Time Valuation solution.

At its core, the feature is versatile: instead of changing a Time Valuation and affecting all history, or cloning a profile to create a parallel universe, admins can now add a new time slice to an individual Time Valuation with a future effective date. The existing version stays as is for all past calculations. The new time slice is activated on the date it's meant to be effective. The hassle of creating clone of time recording profile, mass updating of Job Information and dual maintenance of time recording profile is completely avoided.

And this isn't just about overtime thresholds. The use cases span the full breadth of what Time Valuations do today:

  • Daily and weekly overtime rate changes - when a Time Administrator updates a multiplier from 1.5× to 2.0× 
  • Night shift premium windows - when a shift agreement narrows the qualifying hours from 20:00 to 06:00 to 22:00 to 05:00
  • Break deduction rules - when a works council agreement changes the minimum break duration that counts against working time
  • Non-working day premium rates - when legislation mandates public holiday pay at 2.5× instead of 2.0×
  • Business rule conditions - when FTE eligibility for overtime expands from FTE <= 0.8 to FTE = 1.0
  • Health and safety alerts - when the threshold for a daily working-time warning moves from 10 hours to 12 hours
  • Late-arrival detection - when HR policy increases the tolerance window from 5 minutes to 15 minutes and adjusts the alert trigger from 2 to 3 occurrences per month
  • Multi-country configurations - when Germany and France share a time recording profile, but each has a rule change on a different date

And critically, the retroactive corrections. If an Overtime threshold was set incorrectly at 9 hours when it should have been 8, and this is discovered 15 months later via the Time Valuation Trace tool, the admin corrects the effective-dated slice for January 1, 2025. The system triggers a retroactive recalculation across all 15 months, for all the affected employees.

 

Configuration

The configuration model is intentional in its simplicity. Let me take you through the various scenarios of versioning.

Versioning of Time Valuation

When there is a policy change, the admin navigates to the specific Time Valuation that needs to change — say, the `SPLIT_OT_10` Aggregate & Split Time Valuation that calculates daily overtime. Instead of editing the existing record (which would rewrite history), you add a new version with the effective date of the change.

 

For example:
Version 1 (original): Threshold = 8 hours, valid from the Time Valuation's creation date (01/01/1900)
Version 2 (new): Threshold = 10 hours, effective June 1, 2026

The old version is untouched. The chain of downstream Time Valuations — the ones consuming the output of `SPLIT_OT_10` — needs no reconfiguration. They simply receive whatever the versioned Time Valuation produces on any given calculation date.

This is the key insight of the design: you version at the point of change, not at the top of the chain. Downstream Time Valuations that are not affected by the rule change don't need a new version. Only the Time Valuation where the logic actually differs gets updated.

Handling Cross-Boundary Timesheets

One of the most technically interesting aspects of this feature is how the time valuation engine handles a timesheet that spans a version boundary. Take a weekly timesheet for June 28–July 4, where the overtime threshold changes on July 1.

The system resolves the effective Time Valuation version per processing day when Time Valuation method is Valuate Per Day or Valuate Upto Today:
June 28, 29, 30 → Version 1 (threshold = 8 hours)
July 1, 2, 3, 4 → Version 2 (threshold = 10 hours)

The result is that the correct overtime is calculated for each day, even within a single submission. 

In the Weekly Time Sheet, if the Time Valuation method is Valuate Whole Sheet or Period, the behavior changes. 

The system resolves the effective Time Valuation version with Time Sheet or Period end date which in this case is July 4th. The value of end date of the Time Sheet is considered and calculated with the values as follows:
June 28, 29, 30, July 1, 2, 3, 4 → Version 2 (threshold = 10 hours) 

Retroactive Recalculation

When an error is discovered in a system governing payroll, effective dating enables a clean correction path.

The admin updates the effective version of the Time Valuation that contained the error (for instance, correcting an overtime threshold from 9 hours to 8 hours effective January 1, 2025). This needs just a single recalculation trigger with Time Recording Profile that takes care of a retroactive Time Valuation recalculation for the entire affected period. The Trace tool (Summary of Valuations) provides confirmation of the correction before a payroll rerun is triggered. No individual employee records need updating. No profile changes required. A single administrative action propagates correctly across all affected periods and employees.

Attendance Quota and Effective-Dated Variables

It's worth noting how this capability intersects with Attendance Quota -- a feature that allows employees to request pre-approval for overtime, work from home, or higher duties. When an Attendance Quota Type is configured, the system automatically creates Time Valuation Global Variable Values for Attendance Quota Type "Overtime" (e.g., `DOES_QUOTA_EXIST_OVERTIME`, `TIME_SEGMENTS_OVERTIME`, `WEEKDAY_OVERTIME`, `WORKINGDAY_OVERTIME`). These variables are inherently effective-dated — they reflect the valid period of a specific Attendance Quota request.

This means effective dating operates at two levels: at the configuration level (the Time Valuation itself changing over time) and at the runtime variable level (employee-specific quota windows informing time valuation logic dynamically). Together, they allow a single Attendance Quota Type to serve many employees across different time periods without configuration duplication.

The system handles Time Sheets that straddle a boundary — if a weekly timesheet runs June 28 through July 4 and the Overtime threshold changes on July 1, the engine automatically applies version 1 to June 28–30 and version 2 to July 1–4, within a single timesheet for Time Valuations having valuation method as Valuate Per Day and Valuate Upto Today. 

For Attendance Quota with variable `QUOTA_LIMIT_OVERTIME`, the Time Valuation method used is generally Valuate Whole Sheet or Period. Hence, the end date of the Time Sheet is considered for the calculation of the entire Time Sheet. June 28 - July 4 will use the version 2 values for all calculations.

Results of Time Valuation

Trace

The Time Valuation Trace tool (Summary of Valuations) already provides a window into how time is calculated. Now, it provides the effective dated slices as well.

When a weekly timesheet spans a version boundary (e.g., June 28–July 4 with a July 1 OT change), the trace should clearly show two timelines: the calculation using version 1 for June 28–30 and the calculation using version 2 for July 1–4. For each processing day under a Valuate Per Day method, the trace explicitly states which threshold value was applied.

Payroll auditors, works council representatives, and HR business partners routinely need to explain to employees why their overtime was calculated differently within a single paycheck period. A trace that surfaces the effective-dated timeline removes ambiguity and reduces disputes.

Time Recording Profile Visualization

The broader vision is a visualization layer within the Time Recording Profile that lets admins and HR compare configuration states across time.

With an "As of Date" control, an admin should be able to pull up the Time Valuation configuration as it existed on any date in history — and compare it to how it looks today, or how it will look after a future version activates. The visualization shows inputs, outputs, thresholds, and routing logic side by side across versions.

Limitations

  • Time Valuation method and type cannot be changed. This will raise an error that they have to be same for all effective slices.
  • Create Time Record doesn't support creating more than 1 time slice. 
  • Inactive slices are not allowed and each Time Valuation will always have an effective date 01 Jan 1900 by default.
  • Attendance Quota type cannot be changed in time slices. 

Best Practices for Effective-dated Time Valuation

  • Effective-dated Time Valuation should be used for policy and legal changes where minor changes in threshold, change in input or output time type group, raise messages, factor, etc. This should not be used to change the complete semantic like changing period results from monthly to weekly or visa versa.
  • As Effective-dated Time Valuation uses the end date for all Time Sheet and Period related calculations. Hence, it is important to ensure that you are getting the correct value at boundary conditions. For ex: For a Time Sheet period from June 28, 29, 30, July 1, 2, 3, 4, the calculation will be based on the July 4th time slice which is active. Kindly ensure you this expectation is communicated to stake holders as the results will change for the last week and will not be the same as other weeks when time slice changes on July 1.
  • Refer to the information in 3810718 - Effective Dated Time Valuation - 2H 2026 - SAP for Me for implications on Import of Time Valuation, Integration from 3rd party sources and Reporting.

How Can you request this as an early adopter?

This is an early adopter feature behind a feature toggle. You can request this by reaching out to us. You can reach out to us via your customer success manager, account team or directly to me via SAP community. You can drop me a message in community and we can get connected for this. 

Conclusion

Effective-Dated Time Valuation is one of those features that's hard to explain but immediately understood by anyone who has spent time in the trenches of payroll-adjacent HR configuration.

It doesn't change what Time Valuation calculates. It changes when configuration changes take effect, how they're managed over time, and what happens when the world doesn't cooperate with clean period boundaries.

For the admin who has been cloning profiles every time a collective agreement changes — this removes that entirely.  It also now helps in adding new features with an effective date and don't require to worry about the recalculation that possibly runs for 1 yr or so.

entry.title: 2H2026 Release Update - Role-Based Document View: A Centralized Home for All Employee Documents
entry.content:
Throughout the employee lifecycle — from onboarding to the day they retire — dozens of employment-related documents are created, collected, and stored: employment contracts, performance reviews, work permits, onboarding forms, and many more. But until now, finding any one of these documents in SAP SuccessFactors meant navigating through multiple different modules.

No more.

We're excited to introduce a Role-Based Document View in the latest People Profile — a single, centralized access point for all employee documents, available in the 2H 2026 release of SAP SuccessFactors.

The Problem We're Solving

In SAP SuccessFactors, documents are managed within the modules where they originate — candidate documents in Recruiting, employment documents in Employee Central, and performance-related files in the Talent suite. While each module provides the right context for its content, getting a complete view of an employee’s documents has always required navigating between multiple areas of the system — regardless of your role.

At the same time, viewing a document has traditionally required downloading it first, which can lead to files accumulating on local machines — a potential data security and compliance concern.

The new Role-Based Document View solves both problems.

What's New: One View for All Documents

A new 'Documents' category appears directly in the left-hand navigation of the People Profile. With a single click, users get a complete view of all documents associated with an employee.

The view brings together documents from across the system — work permits, national ID attachments, personal information, background records, performance review attachments, documents from Recruiting — all in one place.

Figure 1: New 'Documents' Category in People Profile

The document view is also available on mobile devices.

To test the mobile experience in your preview environment, please check the following resources for the needed prerequisites:

  • Mobile App Preview Testing Program Supported on iOS and Android
  • 2H 2026 Mobile App Preview Testing Enrollment Now Open

Smart Filtering — Find What You Need

Need to check whether a specific work permit has been uploaded? Or locate a national ID document quickly? The document view includes a category filter that lets you narrow the list, without scrolling through it entirely.

Figure 2: Filtered Document List

Preview Without Downloading

Beyond the centralized document access in the People Profile itself, a second key enhancement in this release is in-system document preview. Previously, clicking on a file triggered an automatic download to the user’s local machine. Now, files open directly in a pop-up preview within the People Profile.

This is a significant win for both productivity and compliance:

  • Download is available when needed, but no longer triggered automatically
  • No more files accumulating on local machines
  • No risk of sensitive employee data being left on a personal device
  • Faster access — no need to open a separate application

Figure 3: New Document Preview with Download Option

Preview is supported for most common file types. For formats where preview is not available, the viewer will open and let you know — with the option to download the file directly from there.

Role-Based Access, Out of the Box

The feature is available to all user types — employees, managers, HR, and administrators — and it fully respects your existing Role-Based Permissions (RBP) configuration. No new permissions need to be set up. Here’s how it works in practice — the document types below are examples just to illustrate the difference; what each user sees depends on your organization’s RBP configuration:

As an employee, you see your own documents — for example your work permit, personal attachments, or national ID records.

Figure 4: Employee Sees All Own Documents

 As a manager, you see documents of your direct reports, which can include attachments uploaded during performance reviews — surfaced directly, without navigating to the performance form.

Figure 5: Manager Sees Documents of Direct Report

As an HR person, you see documents across your area of responsibility. Depending on your RBP setup, this might include employment-related attachments such as work permits, while other document types — like performance review attachments — remain visible only to the responsible manager.

Figure 6: HR Person sees Documents of Person in own Area of Responsibility

 This also extends to internal candidates, contractors, and new hires. An HR person can view an internal candidate’s cover letter, resume, and offer letter flowing in from Recruiting — without ever leaving the People Profile.

What to Keep in Mind

There are two configuration aspects worth reviewing before rollout:

First, the 'Documents'  category in the People Profile is enabled by default — but customers who already rely on a partner document management integration with their own user workspace may want to consider disabling it for now, to avoid presenting end users with a parallel, potentially different view of their documents.

Second, the Documents'  category is available to all employees and roles by default — but you can choose to limit it to specific user groups if needed. Everything else is handled automatically based on your existing RBP permissions — no additional setup required.

Figure 7: Configuration Options 'Documents' Category in Configure Latest People Profile

Current Limitations

Not all documents may appear in the view in every scenario. The following cases are currently not covered:

  • Documents uploaded for dependents
  • Uncategorized documents — stored in custom attachment fields on MDF standard or custom objects without a document category assigned

What This Feature Is Not Designed For

The Role-Based Document View is a read and navigation feature. It is intentionally not designed for:

  • Uploading, deleting, or renaming documents — as these actions typically go hand in hand with updates on the underlying business objects, they remain available only in the corresponding section of the People Profile or the dedicated application UI
  • Displaying documents that are not employee-related, such as company policies or company-wide images managed through the Manage Documents admin UI
  • Replacing a full document management solution or existing partner integrations — rather, the Role-Based Document View is designed to close the gap of not having a central, unified access point to employee documents for roles beyond IT administrators (who previously had access via the Manage Documents admin UI).

What's Coming Next

We recently completed an Early Adopter Care (EAC) program with a motivated group of customers and received very valuable feedback. The planned enhancements below reflect what we heard and plan to address in an upcoming release:

  • Category filter improvements — reducing clutter and making it easier to navigate to the relevant document categories
  • Enhanced filtering capabilities — additional filter options such as filtering by the person who uploaded a document, or by upload date or a specific time range
  • Flag and download multiple documents — flag several documents and download them in one go
  • Read access logging scope — in this first release, all document access is logged regardless of whether documents are marked as PII or confidential; a future enhancement will limit logging to documents explicitly marked as such
  • More granular audit event types — currently, both viewing and downloading a document are logged under the audit event type dataAccess; going forward, viewing will remain dataAccess while downloading will be logged separately as dataExport
  • Uncategorized document support — data migration tools to help customers correct/update uncategorized documents so that they become visible in the new view.

 

We hope the new Role-Based Document View makes navigating employee documents faster and more intuitive — whether you’re an employee checking your own files or an HR person working across a broad population.

Give it a try and let us know what you think — your feedback directly shapes what we build next. Feel free to leave a comment on this blog, and don’t forget to check out our What’s New Viewer and the updated product documentation for further details.

entry.title: 2H 2026 Release Update - What’s New in Document Management Service and OpenText Integration
entry.content:
The SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release brings a meaningful set of enhancements to the Document Management Service (DMS). Improvements span the Manage Documents administration interface, storage accuracy, security, localization, and export capabilities, making it easier for administrators to manage company documents at scale.

This blog covers all DMS enhancements shipping with the 2H 2026 release. Enhancements that apply to all customers are presented first. If your organization uses SAP SuccessFactors integrated with OpenText, the dedicated OpenText sections at the end of this post cover what’s changing for you — including important news about the deprecation of Basic Authentication for the OpenText integration. Customers not using OpenText can stop reading after the general enhancements.

 

General Enhancements

The following enhancements apply to all SAP SuccessFactors customers using Document Management Service, regardless of OpenText integration.

1. Enhancements to the Manage Documents Page

The Manage Documents page in Admin Center has received a fresh, harmonized look and feel in 2H 2026, alongside targeted improvements that address filtering limitations, document metadata inaccuracies, and storage visibility gaps that have been present for some time.

“Filter” and “Advanced Filters” Merged into a Unified Filter Bar

The previous interface had two separate filter sections — “Filter” and “Advanced Filters” — which made it harder to discover and combine filters. In 2H 2026, these are merged into a unified filter bar. A new “Adapt Filters” button lets administrators choose which filters are visible, keeping the bar clean while making all options accessible. The most commonly used filters — Document Name, Status, Uploaded By, Uploaded On, Document Owner, Entity Type, and Document Category — are shown by default. Additional filters can be added via Adapt Filters.

Figure 1: Unified Filter Bar, adjustable via Adapt Filters

New “Uploaded On” Filter

A new date filter allows administrators to filter documents by their upload date — either a specific day or a defined date range. This makes it straightforward to find documents added during a particular time window without scrolling through the full list.

New “Storage Location” Column and Filter

A new Storage Location column and filter has been added to the Documents tab. Possible values are:

  • SuccessFactors — the document is physically stored in SAP SuccessFactors Document Storage.
  • Not Applicable — the document is a dummy replaced file. These files do not consume any storage and have no physical storage location assigned.
  • OpenText (for OpenText-integrated instances only) — the document is stored in OpenText.

For OpenText-integrated instances, this filter is especially useful for identifying which documents remain in SuccessFactors storage and which have already moved to OpenText.

Figure 2: 'Storage Location' added as Filter and Column

Corrected File Size and File Type for Dummy Replaced Files

When a document is replaced in DMS (due to purges or when the instance was updated using the default behavior of the Instance Refresh tool), the system retains a “dummy” placeholder for the original file, so document links will not break. Two long-standing inaccuracies with these placeholder files are corrected in 2H 2026:

  • File size: Dummy replaced files previously showed a file size of 77 KB, which was misleading because these files do not consume any storage. The file size is now correctly shown as 0 Bytes.
  • File type: Dummy replaced files previously always had file type .txt, regardless of what the original document was. This caused issues in UIs that rely on file type to determine rendering behavior — for example, logo images of type .png. Dummy replaced files now “inherit” the file type of the original document.

2. Aligned Metadata Files for Export Document List and Document Bulk Download

The Manage Documents page provides three ways to extract document data in bulk:

  • Export Document List — exports a metadata file listing all documents with their properties.
  • Multi-select download — downloads documents individually selected in the Manage Documents list view, accompanied by a metadata file.
  • Document Bulk Download — downloads the document files themselves, accompanied by a metadata file.

In earlier releases, new metadata fields added to the Manage Documents list view were not always reflected in all of these metadata files, creating an inconsistency between what was visible in the UI and what appeared in the exports. In 2H 2026, the metadata files for Export Document List, Multi-select Download, and Document Bulk Download have been aligned. All current metadata fields shown in the Manage Documents list view — including recently added fields — are now included in all three export files.

Note: For OpenText-integrated instances, the Export Document List metadata file now also includes the OpenText document ID for documents stored in OpenText.

3. Localized Name Field and Bulk Translation for Document Categories

Customers operating in multiple languages can now provide translated labels for custom document categories. The Add and Edit Document Category dialogs in Manage Documents have been extended with a new optional Localized Name field, along with a Translate icon that opens a Translated Languages popup where per-language values can be entered.

Figure 3: New Localized Name field with Translation Icon

 For customers with AI translation enabled, a Bulk Translate button is available in the same dialog. It auto-generates translations for all supported languages based on a source language input, pre-filling the translation fields while keeping them fully editable before saving.

The Localized Name field is pre-populated from the category’s Name field as a convenient starting point. Once a custom localized name is entered, the system protects it — it will not be overwritten if the base Name is later changed.

4. In-System Document Preview

When downloading was the only way to view a document, it created unnecessary friction and compliance risks — files would accumulate on local machines, and sensitive employee data could be left on a personal device even after a brief look.

In 2H 2026, SAP SuccessFactors introduces in-system document preview. Users can now view documents directly within the application without needing to download them. This capability is available both in the People Profile (via the new Role-Based Document View — see the dedicated blog post for that feature) and from the Manage Documents page in Admin Center.

Key benefits:

  • Download is available when needed, but no longer triggered automatically.
  • No more files accumulating on local machines.
  • No risk of sensitive employee data being left on a personal device.
  • Faster access — no need to open a separate application.

Preview is supported for most common file types. For formats where preview is not available, the viewer will open and let you know — with the option to download the file directly.

Figure 4: New Document Preview with Download Option

 Note: The attachment ID naming described in Chapter 5 does not apply to downloads initiated from the document preview widget. The attachment ID is added only for bulk downloads and direct downloads from the Documents tab.

5. Attachment ID Added to Downloaded Document File Names

When multiple users upload documents with the same file name — for example, ten employees each uploading a file called workpermit.jpg — the Manage Documents page can distinguish them by ownership information. But when those files are downloaded, the browser previously saved them all as workpermit.jpg, workpermit(1).jpg, workpermit(2).jpg, and so on, making it impossible to trace which file belongs to whom after the fact.

In 2H 2026, the system appends the unique attachment ID to each file name at download time — placed just before the file extension. This ensures every downloaded file has a globally unique name that can be traced back to the original record in the system.

Note: This applies to bulk downloads and direct downloads from the Documents tab of Manage Documents. Files downloaded via the document preview widget are not affected.

6. Virus Scan for Uploaded Emails with Attachments

The Document Management Service supports uploading .eml and .msg email files. Previously, these files were treated as a single unit — the email file itself was scanned, but the attachments embedded within it were not individually validated or scanned. In 2H 2026, this gap is closed.

When an email file is uploaded to DMS, the system now:

  • Extracts each attachment from the email.
  • Validates whether each attachment’s file type is among the supported types. If any attachment is not a supported file type, the entire upload is rejected with a clear reason.
  • Performs a virus scan for each individual attachment.

This gives administrators stronger content control: disallowed or malicious content embedded in email attachments is caught before it enters the document repository.

Note: Nested email attachments (a child email forwarded as an attachment inside a parent email) are rejected by design to prevent recursive attachment chains.

7. Asynchronous Virus Scan for Large Static Content Files

The Public Content Links tool supports uploading static content files for public distribution. For files over 10 MB, a synchronous virus scan would impose an unacceptable wait on the upload flow. In 2H 2026, the system introduces an asynchronous scanning process for these larger files.

When a file larger than 10 MB is uploaded or replaced through Public Content Links:

  • The file is uploaded to the system immediately.
  • An on-screen message confirms the upload and explains that a background virus scan is underway, with results delivered by email.

Figure 5: On-Screen Message for Asynchronous Virus Scan

  • The Virus Scan Service (VSS) downloads and scans the file in the background.
  • Once complete, the uploader receives an email with the outcome:
  • No virus detected: email with subject ‘Static Content Uploaded’ and a link to access the file.
  • Virus detected: email with subject ‘Virus Detected – File Upload Rejected’; the file is deleted.
  • Scan failure: email with subject ‘Upload Rejected’ asking the user to retry.

This ensures all large static content is properly scanned without blocking the upload experience, and gives administrators a scan outcome notification via email for every file processed.

8. Dynamic Document Count on the Public Content Links Page

A small but practical improvement comes to the Public Content Links page: the Documents section header now shows the total number of uploaded documents currently returned by the list — for example, Documents (234).

Figure 6: New Document Count on the Public Content Links Page

The count is dynamic. It updates automatically based on any active search or filter: if a search reduces results from 500 to 200 documents, the header immediately reflects Documents (200). This removes the need to paginate through the list or count manually to understand how many documents meet given criteria — and makes it easy to verify the impact of filters or recent uploads at a glance.

9. Automated Storage Space Recalculation Jobs for Document Management

Even with best-effort real-time tracking, storage consumption figures can drift over time due to edge cases in uploads, replacements, and deletions. SAP SuccessFactors already had company-level background jobs that periodically recalculate storage consumption. In 2H 2026, user-level recalculation jobs are added as well.

The full set of automated recalculation jobs now includes:

  • Company-level (existing): Recalculate Storage Space for Document Management Service — runs once every 30 days per company.
  • User-level (new in 2H 2026): Recalculate User Storage Space for Document Management Service — runs once every 60 days per user. When triggered, it checks every existing document for a user, sums the total, and updates their current storage figure from scratch. The 60-day frequency (vs. 30-day for company) reflects the higher resource cost of per-user recalculation.

Both jobs follow the same structure — a global scheduler job triggers a per-company job for each tenant. No configuration or manual scheduling is required from administrators. These jobs serve as a periodic safety net, correcting any drift that accumulates over time.

 

For Customers Integrated with OpenText

The following enhancements and notices are relevant only to customers who have SAP SuccessFactors Document Management Service integrated with OpenText.

10. OpenText Document ID Now Included in Export Document List

The Export Document List metadata file now includes the OpenText document ID for each document stored in OpenText, making it straightforward to cross-reference records between SAP SuccessFactors and OpenText directly from the export.

For the full details on the metadata file alignment across all export and download options, see Chapter 2.

11. Improved Document Storage Allocation Values for OpenText-Integrated Instances

For customers using SAP SuccessFactors integrated with OpenText, the Manage Documents page previously provided no visibility into the storage consumed by documents remaining in SAP SuccessFactors Document Storage. In 2H 2026, this changes.

The Document Storage quota on the Manage Documents page now reflects documents physically (still) stored in SAP SuccessFactors Document Storage. Documents residing in OpenText are excluded from this figure, giving administrators an accurate view of the storage consumed within SAP SuccessFactors.

As described in Chapter 1 above, the new ‘Storage Location’ column and filter makes it easy to identify exactly which documents are stored where. For OpenText-integrated instances, filtering by Storage Location = SuccessFactors quickly shows which documents have not yet been migrated — making this feature particularly valuable for customers who are currently running a document migration to OpenText, or planning to start one.

Note: No administrator action is required. The system updates all storage calculations automatically.

12. Action Required: Deprecation of Basic Authentication for OpenText Integration

Basic Authentication for outbound communication from DMS to OpenText is being deprecated and will be deleted on 21 May 2027. Customers must migrate to OAuth 2.0 authentication before this date to avoid disruption to their OpenText integration.

Key milestone dates:

  • End of Development: 14 November 2025 — no new enhancements to Basic Auth.
  • End of Maintenance: 14 May 2026 — SAP no longer fixes bugs for Basic Auth in this integration.
  • Deleted: 21 May 2027 — Basic Authentication is removed and will no longer work.

Starting in 1H 2026, new customers can no longer enable Basic Authentication for the OpenText integration. Customers who switch to OAuth 2.0 cannot switch back. A warning banner has been added to the Admin Center configuration page to alert administrators still using Basic Authentication.

Why migrate to OAuth 2.0?

  • Stronger security with token-based access rather than reusable passwords.
  • Improved compliance with modern authentication standards.
  • Lower risk of credential compromise.
  • Support for long-lived certificates and automated expiry reminders.

Note: This deprecation applies specifically to outbound communication from DMS to OpenText. Inbound communication from OpenText to SAP SuccessFactors already uses OAuth 2.0 and is not affected. To migrate, follow the steps in ‘Upgrade to OAuth 2.0 Authentication with OpenText’ in the SAP Help Portal.

For more details, please visit the blog post: 2H 2025 Release - OAuth 2.0 & Improved Document Migration for SuccessFactors to OpenText integration

entry.title: 2H 2026 Release Update — What’s New in Business Rules
entry.content:
The SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release brings a focused set of enhancements to the Business Rules engine. A performance-relevant improvement to the lookup function reduces the need for redundant configurations, two new rule functions close long-standing gaps in data type handling, and quality-of-life changes to variable editing and the MDF Sequence object make day-to-day rule authoring smoother.

This blog covers all five Business Rules enhancements shipping with the 2H 2026 release.

1. Return Complete Object Information in Rule Engine Lookup Function

Previously, when you needed values from multiple fields of the same object in a rule, you had to write a separate lookup expression for each field. For rules that reference MDF objects with several relevant fields, this quickly produced long and repetitive configurations — and every additional lookup expression added performance overhead.

In 2H 2026, the Rule Engine lookup function has been enhanced with a new lookup object option. When you select the lookup object as the field parameter in a lookup expression, the function returns the complete object instance with all its fields, rather than the value of a single field. To make the best use of this enhancement you can assign this object instance to a variable and then reference individual fields from that variable throughout the rule, replacing what previously required multiple separate lookups with a single expression.

Figure 1: Example of Lookup the whole object "Insurance Plan Rates" to use different fields of the lookup object in the Rule Definition

Note: This enhancement delivers significant performance improvements for organizations that rely on object lookups, reducing the need to create multiple lookups to retrieve different fields from the same object.

2. Get Enum Value As String — New Rule Function

Enum fields and string fields are incompatible types in business rules — you cannot assign an enum value directly to a string field. This is a common friction point when transferring data from MDF or EC standard fields to custom MDF fields: standard fields can be of type enum, but custom MDF fields cannot. Previously, there was no supported way to bridge this gap in a business rule.

In 2H 2026, a new Get Enum Value As String rule function is available. It takes an enum field as input and returns its technical value as a string, which can then be assigned to a string field, used in a comparison, or passed to another expression.

Figure 2: Example of using the Get Enum Value As String function to map a standard field of type enum to a custom field of type string

Note: The function returns the technical enum value — not the localized display label and not a picklist code.

3. Get Translated Text — New Rule Function

MDF fields of type translatable hold translated text for multiple locales, but that translated text cannot be used directly where a string value is required. To work around this, rule authors previously had to build a conditional rule structure with a separate branch for each supported language — checking the user’s locale and returning hardcoded text for each case. The result was long, hard-to-maintain rules that needed to be updated every time a new language was added.

Figure 3: Example of a former needed comprehensive rule definition to get the label of Company Benefit Type (field type translatable) in the users language

In 2H 2026, a new Get Translated Text rule function is available for MDF objects with 'Translatable' fields. It retrieves the translated text of a localized field in the current user’s locale and returns it as a string. To use it, specify the translated field in the Translated Field parameter of the new function. The rule evaluates the correct translation at runtime for each user automatically.

 

Figure 4: Example of getting the label of Company Benefit Type (field type translatable) always in the users local, using the Get Translated Text function

Note: If no translation exists in the user’s locale, the function falls back to the company locale, then to the default value.

4. Editable Variables in Business Rules

Variables in business rules previously became locked as soon as they were used in the rule configuration. To change a variable’s definition, all references to it had to be removed from the rule configuration first — only once the variable was no longer used anywhere in the rule could it be edited. After making the change, every reference had to be added back manually. The same locked state also created a blind spot in rule diagnostics: when a rule produced warnings, the system could indicate that a warning existed but could not highlight the specific variable responsible.

In 2H 2026, variables used in the body of a business rule can be edited at any time. The edit icon is now active for in-use variables, allowing the value expression to be updated directly. When editing a variable, the type cannot be changed (if the variable is a number, it remains a number) and the interface limits the available fields and rule functions accordingly to prevent mismatches. The warning highlighting improvement is included automatically: the system can now mark the specific variable causing a warning, making troubleshooting faster.

Figure 5: New edit-option for variables used in the rule configuration

Note: This feature originated from (Customer Community Idea 329255).

5. MDF Sequence Object Enhancements

The MDF Sequence object, used to generate sequential values in business configurations, previously displayed all-English technical labels — regardless of the language the system was running in. For customers operating in languages other than English, this created unnecessary friction when searching for and working with the Sequence object in tools such as Manage Data and Configure Object Definition. The field representing the upcoming sequence value was also labeled Current, which was ambiguous: it actually holds the next value to be assigned, not the last value that was used.

In 2H 2026, the Sequence object receives two improvements:

  • Translatable labels: All field labels in the Sequence object — including the object name itself — are now translatable. They display in the user’s language, bringing the Sequence object in line with the rest of the Metadata Framework.
  • Renamed field: The Current field has been renamed to Next Value, which accurately reflects what the field contains: the value that will be assigned the next time the sequence is incremented.
 
Figure 6: Example of translated fields and renamed "Next Value" field in Sequence Object
Note: Because the object name itself is now translated, non-English users will need to search for the Sequence object using its translated name in Manage Data and Configure Object Definition.
