entry.title: HCM Procss and Forms Efficient F4 Input Help: Triggering Database Reads Only When Required
entry.content:
The Problem

When configuring F4 input help in an HCM P&F form, there can be two common challenges when the F4 values are retrieved from large database tables.

First, unnecessary database reads can impact the overall form load time.

When a generic service is used to provide the F4 values, the service method can be called during form initialization as well as when the user actually clicks the F4 help.

If the database SELECT is executed every time the service is called, the system performs a database read even though the user has not requested the F4 help yet. With large volumes of data, these unnecessary reads can increase the form's initialization time.

Second, the F4 values may need to be filtered based on other fields on the form.

In many business scenarios, displaying all possible values in an F4 help is not desirable. The values should be restricted based on information the user has already entered or selected in other fields.

For example, if one field contains a Company Code and another field provides an F4 help for Cost Center, the F4 help should ideally display only the Cost Centers relevant to the selected Company Code.

This means that the F4 help needs to:

  • Avoid unnecessary database reads during form initialization.

  • Execute the database read only when the user requests the F4 help.

  • Dynamically filter the F4 values based on other field values available on the form.

So, how can we configure the process to achieve all three?

The Approach

The solution is to make the database read conditional and on demand by handling it within the GET_HELP_VALUES method of the generic service class.

The GET_HELP_VALUES method can be called during different stages of the form processing. Instead of executing the database SELECT every time the method is called, we can check the event and field name to determine whether the call was triggered by an actual F4 request.

When the form is initialized, the generic service may be called, but the database SELECT is skipped.

Additionally, the SERVICE_FIELD_VALUES parameter of GET_HELP_VALUES can be used to access values from other fields on the form. These values can then be used as selection criteria in the database query, allowing the F4 results to be dynamically filtered.

The Implementation

Let's configure the process step by step.

Step 1: Define the Operation and Field Group

Under your generic service, define the required operation say GET_HELP and field group.

 

Step 2: Define the Field for the F4 Help

Define the field in generic service for which the input help needs to be provided and assign the GET_HELP operation defined in the previous step.

 

Step 3: Maintain the Input Help and Data Binding

Configure the input help and maintain the appropriate data binding for the field.

 

Step 4: Configure the User Event

Configure the user event that will be triggered when the F4 help is requested.

 

Step 5: Maintain the Fields for the User Event

Maintain the fields required for the user event.

For example, if ZGET_HELP is the field for which the input help is required, maintain this field in the user event configuration. 

Also include the field ZINPUT which has to be used as filter for SELECT.

 

 

 

Step 6: Maintain the Metadata

In the metadata configuration:

  • Select Has Value Help.

  • F4 Parent field should be configured

  • Maintain SH=*** along with the name of the operation defined earlier.

  • SH represents the Search Help. 

Once these configurations are in place, we can move to the generic service implementation.

The Code

Now comes the important part — making the database read conditional.

In the IF_HRASR00GEN_SERVICE~GET_HELP_VALUES method, check the event and the field name before executing the database SELECT.

The key point is to ensure that the SELECT is executed only when the event corresponds to GET_HELP and the requested field is the field for which the input help is configured.

This prevents the database read from being executed unnecessarily during form initialization.

 

 

Important: Make sure that the field name used in the condition matches the field name maintained in the generic service configuration.

 

You can also use values from other fields on the form to further restrict the database query. The SERVICE_FIELD_VALUES parameter can be used to retrieve the selected field values and apply them as filters in your SELECT statement.

In the above image, “Get Help On Demand” (with technical name GET_HELP_FIELD in SAP_PA corresponds to ZGET_HELP)is the field configured for the F4 input help, while “Filter for F4”  (with technical name ZINPUT)is the field whose value is used as the filter criterion for the F4 results.

METHOD if_hrasr00gen_service~get_help_values.

DATA: lv_filter_value TYPE string.

"Read the value of another field from the form
READ TABLE service_field_values
ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_field>)
WITH KEY fieldname = 'ZINPUT'.

IF sy-subrc = 0.
lv_filter_value = <ls_field>-fieldvalue.
ENDIF.

"Execute the SELECT only when F4 is requested
IF event = 'GET_HELP'
AND <help_datasets_wa>-fieldname = 'GET_HELP_FIELD'.

SELECT ...
FROM ...
INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_help_values)
WHERE ... = @LV_filter_value.

ENDIF.

ENDMETHOD.

 

In this example, GET_HELP_FIELD is the field for which the F4 help is configured, while ZINPUT is another field whose value is used as a filter criterion. The SELECT is executed only when the GET_HELP event is triggered, and the value from ZINPUT is used to dynamically filter the F4 results.

The Result

With this configuration, the generic service can still be called during form initialization, but the database SELECT is not executed unnecessarily.

The database read happens only when the user actually requests the F4 input help.

This provides two important benefits:

  • Reduced form initialization time by avoiding unnecessary database reads.

  • Improved database performance by executing the SELECT only when the data is actually required.

Additionally, the F4 values can be dynamically filtered using other field values from the form through SERVICE_FIELD_VALUES.

In this way, we avoid unnecessary and duplicate database reads while keeping the F4 input help dynamic and on demand.

entry.title: Introducing Time Account Balance Access in Time Valuation: More Flexibility, More Control
entry.content:
Why This Feature Matters

Customer and partner feedback plays an important role in shaping SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking. The need to combine time account balances with time valuation logic was raised in numerous customer and partner discussions and was also reflected in an Influence Request, highlighting the demand for a standard solution.

Many organizations have working time rules that depend not only on recorded working time, but also on the current balance of a time account. Until now, time account balances were not available directly within time valuation processing. As a result, scenarios that required valuation decisions based on an account balance could not be implemented in time valuations.

With the introduction of Time Account Balance in Time Valuation, SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking addresses this requirement by enabling account balances to be considered directly within the time valuation process.

 

Introducing Time Account Balance in Time Valuation

The new functionality is delivered through a new Valuation Type called Valuation Function.

Within this valuation type, the new Valuation Function "Get Time Account Balance" can be selected. The function retrieves the balance of a configured account and makes it available for subsequent valuation steps.

Depending on the business requirement, balances can be retrieved from:

  • Working Time Accounts (WTA)
  • Time Off in Lieu (TOIL) accounts
  • Attendance Quotas

The account is selected using its Time Account Category. When retrieving an Attendance Quota balance, the corresponding Attendance Quota Type must additionally be specified.

The returned balance can then be evaluated against thresholds, compared with recorded time, or used as an input for further valuation logic.

 

Typical Business Scenarios

The ability to access account balances directly within a time valuation enables several scenarios that previously could not be implemented within standard valuation logic.

The following examples illustrate some of the most common requirements discussed with customers, partners, and consultants.

 

Early Warning Before Reaching an Account Limit

Many organizations maintain upper limits for working time accounts. While the actual limit handling is usually managed within Time Off, there is often a business requirement to inform employees before the limit is reached.

A typical example is a working time account with a maximum balance of 180 hours. Instead of waiting until the account reaches the limit, the organization may want to notify employees once they approach a predefined threshold, such as 160 hours.

This enables a traffic-light approach:

  • Green: Balance below the warning threshold
  • Yellow: Balance approaching the limit
  • Red: Account limit reached

By considering the current account balance within a time valuation, warning time can be identified and processed before the actual account limit is exceeded.

While the example above focuses on a positive balance threshold, the same principle can also be applied to negative account balances and lower limits.

 

Preventing a Negative Account Balance

Another common requirement is to prevent time consumption that would result in a negative account balance.

To support this process, the valuation effectively needs to simulate the resulting account balance by combining the current balance with the requested consumption. If the resulting balance would become negative, the consumption can be prevented accordingly.

The account balance therefore becomes an essential input for the validation process.

 

Sequential Consumption Across Multiple Accounts

Many organizations use multiple time accounts to manage different categories of accumulated time.

A common example is the combination of:

  • Working Time Account (WTA)
  • Time Off in Lieu (TOIL)

In these scenarios, balances often need to be consumed in a predefined sequence.

For example, available balances should first be deducted from the Working Time Account. Only after the WTA balance has been completely consumed should further deductions be applied to the TOIL account.

This requires the valuation process to evaluate the current balance of the first account before determining how the remaining consumption should be processed.

 

How It Works in a Nutshell

The new functionality is delivered through the Valuation Type "Valuation Function" and the Valuation Function "Get Time Account Balance" introduced earlier.

After selecting the valuation function, consultants specify the account for which the balance should be determined by choosing the corresponding Time Account Category. When Attendance Quota is selected, the corresponding Attendance Quota Type must additionally be specified.

Example configuration using Time Account Balance in Time Valuation

For each processed day, the valuation determines the balance available at the end of the previous day.

In addition, manual adjustments and other direct postings that exist for the processed day are considered when calculating the returned balance. The only exception are postings generated by time valuations.

This distinction is important because valuation-generated postings may have been created during an earlier time valuation run. Including these postings could lead to inconsistent results during recalculation scenarios.

By excluding valuation-generated postings and independently determining the relevant balance for each processing run, the valuation effectively simulates the account balance that should be used for the current evaluation.

The resulting balance is provided in the configured Time Type Group Above.

Optionally, a Time Type Group Below can be configured. This group contains the sum of all direct account postings for the processed day, excluding postings generated by time valuations.

In summary:

  • Time Type Group Above contains the opening balance for the processed day, calculated as the previous day's closing balance plus all direct postings of the processed day, excluding postings generated by time valuations.
  • Time Type Group Below contains only the direct postings of the processed day, again excluding postings generated by time valuations.

Providing the direct postings separately allows customers to distinguish between the balance carried forward from the previous day and same-day adjustments. For example, a subsequent time valuation can subtract Time Type Group Below from Time Type Group Above to derive a balance that excludes the processed day's direct postings.

 

Configuration Examples

 

A Note About the Configuration Examples

Before diving into the configuration examples, it is important to keep in mind that each example focuses on a specific building block and intentionally isolates only the aspects that are relevant for demonstrating the use of the new functionality.

In real customer implementations, time valuations are typically part of larger Time Recording Profiles that often contain numerous existing valuations, account posting rules, alerts, and other customer-specific requirements. As a result, the examples shown below should not be considered complete end-to-end solutions. Instead, they are intended to illustrate the principle of how Time Account Balance in Time Valuation can be used to address specific business requirements.

Depending on the customer's requirements, collective agreements, legal regulations, and existing configuration, the examples might need to be adapted or integrated differently into the overall Time Recording Profile. In some cases, alternative designs may even be more suitable for a particular customer scenario.

For that reason, the following examples should be viewed as implementation patterns that demonstrate the capabilities of the new functionality rather than recommended reference configurations for productive use.

 

Configuration Example 1: Early Warning Before Reaching an Account Limit

 

Solution in a Nutshell

The objective of this example is to inform employees before a predefined Working Time Account threshold is reached.

In the example, the employee's daily working time difference is first calculated. In parallel, the current Working Time Account balance is retrieved using the new Get Time Account Balance valuation function.

The account balance and the calculated daily difference are then aggregated in a subsequent valuation step. Once the configured threshold is reached or exceeded, a warning message is generated and displayed to the employee.

This approach allows organizations to implement a traffic-light style monitoring process, helping employees take action before the actual account limit is reached.

The example focuses on illustrating the use of the new Get Time Account Balance functionality. In productive implementations, additional valuation steps, customer-specific rules, or existing valuation logic may need to be considered.

Complete configuration of Example 1 using Time Account Balance in Time Valuation

 

About This Example

In the configuration shown above, the warning is evaluated and generated on a daily basis. As a result, the same warning message may be displayed on multiple consecutive days once the threshold has been reached.

Depending on the business requirement, the design can be refined further. For example, the daily result stored in TEMP2 can be accumulated in a monthly time container and the warning logic can be moved to a monthly aggregation. This allows the message to be shown less frequently while still informing employees that a threshold has been reached.

 

Configuration Example 2: Preventing a Negative Account Balance

 

Solution in a Nutshell

The objective of this example is to prevent time consumption that would reduce a Working Time Account balance below zero.

The configuration first determines the employee's daily working time difference. In parallel, the current Working Time Account balance is retrieved using the new Get Time Account Balance valuation function.

Both values are then combined in a subsequent aggregation valuation. The valuation effectively simulates the resulting account balance by considering both the current account balance and the posting that would be created by the recorded time.

If the resulting balance falls below zero, an ALERT_AND_UI_ERROR message is raised, and the recording cannot be saved. This allows organizations to enforce a strict "no negative balance" policy directly within the time valuation process.

The example focuses on illustrating the use of the new Get Time Account Balance functionality. In productive implementations, additional valuation steps, customer-specific rules, or existing valuation logic may need to be considered before integrating the configuration into an overall Time Recording Profile.

Complete configuration of Example 2 using Time Account Balance in Time Valuation

 

About This Example

Unlike the threshold warning scenario shown in the previous example, repeated message displays are typically not a concern here.

Once the validation determines that the requested consumption would result in a negative account balance, the recording is prevented from being saved through an error message. As a result, the employee is expected to see the message only for the recording that violates the rule, making additional measures to limit the frequency of the message unnecessary.

 

Configuration Example 3: Sequential Consumption Across Multiple Accounts

 

Solution in a Nutshell

This example demonstrates how time consumption can be deducted from multiple accounts in a predefined sequence. The actual account consumption logic is relatively straightforward. However, in order to create a complete and realistic example, the configuration also includes logic that determines how overtime is distributed between the Working Time Account (WTA) and the Time Off in Lieu (TOIL) account.

For demonstration purposes, the example uses a simple rule:

  • Daily overtime up to 2 hours is posted to the Working Time Account.
  • Daily overtime exceeding 2 hours is posted to the Time Off in Lieu account.

As a result, a significant part of the configuration is dedicated to determining the destination account for newly generated overtime postings rather than the actual consumption process.

The visualization below therefore contains two distinct areas:

1. Overtime Account Assignment

The left-hand side of the configuration calculates the daily working time difference and determines whether overtime should be posted to the Working Time Account or the TOIL account. In this example, the Overtime Split valuation separates overtime above and below a threshold of two hours, resulting in postings to different accounts.

2. Sequential Account Consumption

The right-hand side contains the functionality that is relevant for this blog post.

The Get Time Account Balance valuation retrieves the current Working Time Account balance and provides it for subsequent valuation steps. Based on that balance, the Consumption WTA valuation determines whether the requested consumption can be covered completely by the Working Time Account or whether part of the consumption must be redirected.

If sufficient balance is available in the Working Time Account, the complete consumption is deducted from the WTA. If the balance is not sufficient, the remaining amount is routed to the TOIL account and deducted there instead. This allows the accounts to be consumed in a predefined sequence without manual intervention.

Complete configuration of Example 3 using Time Account Balance in Time Valuation

 

About This Example

The configuration shown here was intentionally created as a simple demonstration scenario and should not be interpreted as a recommended overtime design.

The rule that posts overtime up to two hours into a Working Time Account and any additional overtime into a TOIL account was chosen only to generate balances in two different accounts and thereby illustrate the sequential consumption concept.

The actual consumption logic itself requires only a relatively small portion of the overall configuration. Most of the complexity shown in the diagram originates from the example-specific posting logic used to create the account balances.

The concept is not limited to two accounts. The same approach can be extended to additional accounts if required. Furthermore, the pattern can also be applied to scenarios involving Attendance Quotas, enabling sequential consumption across different balance types depending on customer requirements.

 

Restrictions and Considerations

As with any new functionality, there are a few considerations that should be taken into account when designing and implementing solutions based on Time Account Balance in Time Valuation.

 

No Automatic Recalculation Trigger for Direct Account Changes

Changes made directly to a time account, such as manual adjustments, do not automatically trigger a recalculation.

As a result, valuation results that depend on a time account balance are not automatically recalculated when account balances are modified outside the regular time evaluation process.

If such changes should be reflected in time valuation results, the relevant recalculation must be triggered manually.

 

Daily Time Valuations Only

The functionality is designed for daily valuation processing and is currently supported only in daily time valuations.

Time valuations configured with the Valuate Whole Sheet or Period valuation method are not supported.

When designing valuation logic that depends on account balances, consultants should therefore ensure that the relevant processing takes place within a daily valuation chain.

 

Mass Recording Considerations

When employees record time for a period longer than a single day using Mass Recording, alerts or warning messages based on account balances may not be visible immediately after saving the recordings.

A typical example is the early warning scenario described earlier in this blog. If an employee records time for multiple future days in a single action and thereby reaches a configured threshold, the corresponding alert may not be displayed directly after the recording is saved.

 

Summary

The new Time Account Balance in Time Valuation functionality extends the flexibility of SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking by making account balances available directly within the valuation process.

This allows valuation logic to combine recorded working time, intermediate valuation results, and the current balance of a Working Time Account, Time Off in Lieu account, or Attendance Quota within the same time valuation chain.

As a result, new business scenarios such as early warning thresholds, negative balance prevention, and sequential account consumption can now be implemented within standard time valuation logic.

For consultants and implementation teams, the feature provides a powerful new building block that can be incorporated into existing valuation chains and used to address customer requirements that previously could not be realized within time valuations.

 

New to Time Valuation?

If you would like to learn more about the fundamentals of Time Valuation and how valuation rules are used to process recorded working times, I also recommend starting with the following overview blog post, which provides a solid introduction to the concept and its key building blocks: How to Setup Time Evaluation in Time Tracking

 

Looking for More Time Valuation Innovations?

Time Account Balance in Time Valuation is only one of the recent enhancements in SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking.

Another significant innovation is the introduction of effective-dated Time Valuations, which allows time valuation configurations to be maintained with validity periods and helps reduce the need to clone Time Recording Profiles when valuation requirements change.

If you are interested in learning more about this capability, I highly recommend taking a look at the blog post by my colleague:

Say goodbye to cloning policy changed time recording profile! Effective-dated Time Valuation is here

Together, these enhancements further increase the flexibility of SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking and provide additional options for designing and maintaining time valuation logic.

 

Share Your Feedback

The scenarios described in this blog represent only a subset of the requirements discussed with customers, partners, and consultants.

If you are already evaluating potential use cases for this new functionality, or if you have additional scenarios that could benefit from Time Account Balance in Time Valuation, I would be happy to hear from you.

Please feel free to share your thoughts, experiences, and questions in the comments section below. Your feedback helps us better understand customer requirements and continue improving SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking.

entry.title: 2H 2026 Release Update - Provisioning Settings Are Moving to Admin Center
entry.content:
As part of our ongoing efforts to simplify system administration and provide a more consistent experience, we are migrating approximately 150 configuration settings from Provisioning UI portal to SAP SuccessFactors Admin Center.

This transition brings commonly used configuration settings into Admin Center, making them easier for administrators to access and manage.

Why Are We Making This Change?

Historically, several SAP SuccessFactors configuration settings have been available only through Provisioning UI, primarily accessed by SAP Support and authorized implementation partners.

This required customers to seek external assistance for certain configuration changes, adding additional steps to routine administrative activities.

By moving these settings to Admin Center, we aim to:

  • Simplify administration: Consolidate configuration settings within the familiar Admin Center experience.

  • Improve accessibility: Allow authorized administrators to view and manage supported settings directly.

  • Reduce dependencies: Minimize the need to engage SAP Support or implementation partners for routine configuration changes.

What's Changing in the 2H 2026 Release?

As part of the 2H 2026 release, we are progressively migrating approximately 150 Provisioning settings to Admin Center.

These settings span multiple SAP SuccessFactors product areas and will be accessible to administrators with the appropriate permissions.

The migration focuses on improving the administrative experience while preserving existing configuration behavior.

What Does This Mean for Customers?

With these settings available in Admin Center, customers can expect:

  • Centralized configuration management: Access more administrative settings from a single location.

  • Greater operational efficiency: Make supported configuration changes without additional coordination with SAP Support or implementation partners.

  • Consistent user experience: Manage configurations through the familiar Admin Center interface.

What Happens to Existing Configurations?

Existing configurations will be preserved as part of the migration. Customers will not need to recreate or manually migrate their settings.

The primary change is where these settings are accessed and managed, rather than how the underlying configurations function.

What's Next in 1H 2027?

In 1H 2027, we plan to remove the "migrated settings" from the legacy Provisioning UI portal, further consolidating configuration management within Admin Center.

What Should Administrators Do?

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review the 2H 2026 release documentation to identify settings available in Admin Center. Replacement of Provisioning Settings with Admin Center Settings: 2H 2026 Batch | SAP Help Portal

  • Familiarize themselves with the updated configuration experience.

  • Ensure that appropriate administrator permissions are assigned.

Looking Ahead

Migrating Provisioning settings to Admin Center is another step toward a simpler, more consistent SAP SuccessFactors administration experience.

By consolidating configuration capabilities, we aim to make system management more accessible and efficient while reducing the complexity of day-to-day administration.

Time off capabilities in the HR Service Assistant

Consolidated time sheet in SAP S/4 HANA Cloud Public Edition

entry.title: When I ask Joule something, what actually happens behind the scenes?
entry.content:
At first glance it may feel like you are simply chatting with an AI assistant. In reality there is an intelligent orchestration layer working behind the scenes to ensure every response is accurate, secure and connected to your business systems. Let's break it down.

Step 1: Everything starts with the user - Every interaction begins with a person. There are two ways a user can interact with AI:

  • Through Joule by asking a question (for example, "Who hasn't completed their performance review?")
  • Directly inside SAP SuccessFactors (HCM) by clicking an action, such as approving leave or updating employee information. Both paths eventually lead to the same AI engine.

Step 2: Joule or HCM sends the request to the Agent Runtime - The Agent Runtime acts like the brain or orchestrator. Instead of immediately generating an answer, it first plans the best way to fulfil the request.

  • Its job is to understand the request and decide: What information is needed?, Which systems should be contacted?, Which tools should be used?, Is the user authorized to perform this action?

Step 3: Agent Configuration decides how the request should be handled - Inside the Agent Runtime are three important components.

  1. Agent Config - This is the AI's instruction manual. It defines: which agent should respond, what workflow to follow and which business rules apply.
  2. A2A Client (Agent-to-Agent) - Sometimes one AI agent cannot complete the task alone. t may need help from another specialized agent. It defines: one agent understands HR policies, another specializes in recruiting and another handles payroll.
  3. MCP Client - The MCP Client connects AI with enterprise systems. Instead of creating separate integrations for every application MCP provides one standard way to communicate with: SAP applications, databases, APIs, documents, custom enterprise systems

Step 4: Selecting the right tools - Once the runtime understands the request, it chooses the most suitable tool. The user never needs to choose these tools manually. Joule automatically selects the best one.

  • It might use: Calculator, Web Search, SAP Joule Functions, Custom enterprise applications, MCP-connected enterprise tools

Step 5: Large Language Models (LLM) do the reasoning - Once all the required information is collected, everything is sent to the Large Language Model (LLM). This is where AI actually thinks to generate an intelligent response.

  • The LLM combines: your question, enterprise data, tool outputs, business context,

Step 6: Agent Services keep everything secure - While all of this happens, another layer called Agent Services continuously monitors the process. It provides:

  • Guardrails – ensures AI follows company policies.
  • Metering – tracks resource usage.
  • Tracing – records what happened during each request.
  • Benchmarking – measures performance and quality.
  • Extensibility – allows organizations to add new capabilities in the future.

This architecture shows that Joule is much more than a chatbot. It acts as an intelligent coordinator that understands your request, connects to the right enterprise systems, collaborates with specialized AI agents, uses the appropriate tools, reasons with Large Language Models and delivers secure, governed and business-aware responses all within a unified AI framework.

entry.title: Already-Posted Off-Cycle Result Re-selected? How Simulation Run Behaves
entry.content:
Introduction

Recently, I raised a question in the SAP Community about payroll posting for a terminated employee. I have since found the answer, and I’m sharing it here in case you run into the same behaviour.

Original question: Solved: Off-cycle payroll result for terminated employee r... - SAP Community

The Scenario

  • We processed an off-cycle payroll run for a terminated employee and posted it to Finance successfully.
  • The FI document was created, and the posting run status showed “Documents Posted".
  • Later, we ran the regular monthly payroll posting for all employees in the same payroll area.
  • The terminated employee had no new regular payroll result for the period, which is expected since he was terminated.
  • Even so, the regular posting run selected the same off-cycle result that had already been posted. It looked as if the system was trying to post it again.

What We Checked First

  1. The employee was not locked at any point.
  2. No retroactive calculation was triggered after the off-cycle posting, so no new payroll result was generated.
  3. The original off-cycle posting document was not reversed or cancelled.
  4. The behavior was reproduced in our test/dev system as well.

Nothing in the data pointed to a problem, so I asked whether this was a known issue and whether there was a standard way to resync without reversing the original posting or creating a duplicate.

What the Posting Run Showed

In the posting item evaluation, the statistics showed:

Selected: 3 personnel numbers
Evaluated: 2
Rejected: 0
Skipped: 1

The third personnel number, the terminated employee, was flagged with a warning instead of being evaluated like the others. Opening the message gave this:

Payroll result has already been evaluated in run 0000023794

So the employee was selected for the period, but the system recognized that the result had already been evaluated in the earlier posting run and skipped it.

The Solution

The behavior was not an error. It comes from how the simulation run works.

The simulation run does not primarily validate whether a personnel number has already been posted in a previous posting run. Instead, it simulates the posting of the payroll results selected for the specified payroll period.

The simulation option only prevents the creation of a new posting run and FI document. It does not act as a filter to exclude employees whose payroll results have already been posted.

So when the terminated employee appeared in the selection, that didn’t mean the system would post him a second time. The selection showed everything that fell within the period, including a result that had already been posted.

What Happened in the Live Run

When we executed the live posting run, the system posted only the correct amount. There was no duplicate posting and no need to reverse the original document or resync anything.

Key Takeaways

Being selected is not the same as being posted. An employee can appear in the selection and still be skipped.

  • Don’t use the simulation output as a duplicate check.
  • Simulation only suppresses the new posting run and FI document. It does not exclude results that were already posted.
    Read the message on the skipped employee. “Payroll result has already been evaluated in run …” tells you which earlier run holds the result.
  • The live run determines what is actually posted. In our case, only the correct amount was posted.
  • Verify after the live run. Confirm the new posting run and its FI documents, and check that the earlier off-cycle FI document is unchanged.

Conclusion

If an already-posted off-cycle result for a terminated employee shows up again in a later posting run, don’t assume a duplicate will be created, and don’t reverse the original posting because of what the selection shows. Check the message on the skipped employee, run the live posting, and verify the resulting documents.

I hope this saves you some troubleshooting time. If you have seen similar behavior or know more about the selection logic behind it, please share it in the comments.

entry.title: Personnel Calculation Rule - Factoring Parameter
entry.content:
Introduction

Accurate payroll execution is the backbone of employee life cycle management, and ensuring employees are compensated precisely for days worked—while factoring in complex absence structures—is a critical daily challenge for SAP consultants. In this blog post, we will walk through a practical Personnel Calculation Rule (PCR) that bridges Time Management and Payroll by leveraging variables like TKSOLL and TKAP to determine exact calendar days worked and streamline wage type valuation.

Importance of PCR:

In an employee life cycle payroll plays a major role. Generally an employee gets paid for the number of days worked in a particular payroll period/cycle. Payroll calculations takes place based company policy. Here let's take a scenario where they excludes paid absence and finds exact calendar days an employee worked in a particular period

Operations used:

TKSOLL - Takes planned working time in Calendar days.

TKAP** - Paid absence in Calendar days.

PCR Syntax:

*

XXXX

RTE=TKSOLL       * Sets rate to planned calendar days

RTE-TKAP**       * Subtracts unpaid absences

ADDWT *          * Adds wage type to output table

PCR Image:

Explanation:

  • In the above sample PCR we initially check for the wagetype which needs to be processed.
  • Then we set Rate equals to TKSOLL, which means the rate is equal to number of calendar days in planned working time. This varies from employee to employee based on the work schedule which is assigned to them. The work schedule determines the working time/shift of an employee with breaks, public holidays configured in it.
  • Then the rate is being subtracted by the paid absence with counting class 06 followed by paid absence with counting class 07 and 09.
  • Finally stores the calculated Rate in the wage type which is being processed.

Conclusion:

Mastering payroll factoring through custom PCRs gives you the flexibility to meet organizational policies by utilizing TKSOLL for planned calendar days and subtracting paid absences via TKAP to reflect true working times. Implementing this approach improves accuracy and transparency across your payroll and time management modules, so feel free to share your thoughts, questions, or alternative approaches in the comments below.

entry.title: Implementing Dynamic Approvals in SAP SmartRecruiter
entry.content:
The Problem: Static Approval Chains

By default, SmartRecruiter allows you to configure Sequential or Parallel approval chains where the list of approvers is fixed at configuration time. This works well for homogeneous workflows, but breaks down when business rules require different approvers based on runtime data.

Two scenarios that call for dynamic routing:

  • Job approval: If the total compensation package is >= 100 (e.g., LPA), it must be approved by User A and User B; otherwise, by User A and User C.
  • Offer approval: If the salary hike is <= 50%, approvers are A and B; if 50–100%, approvers are A, B, and C; if > 100%, approvers are A, B, and the Head of Department.

These rules cannot be pre-configured statically. The solution is an Integration-type approval chain that delegates control to an external CPI flow at runtime.

Setting Up an Integration-Type Approval Chain in SmartRecruiter

Navigate to Settings > Job Approvals in SmartRecruiter and create a new approval chain. Instead of selecting Sequential or Parallel, choose the Integration tab. This tells SmartRecruiter that an external integration (your CPI iFlow) is responsible for managing the approval process.

Inside the chain configuration, set the Approval Chain type to Integration and select your registered CPI application as the App Integration. All scope fields can be set to 'All selected' for a global rule or scoped down as needed.

Key concept: When an Integration-type chain is active, SmartRecruiter assigns a system/integration user as the initial placeholder approver. This user acts as a signal to your CPI flow that the approval needs to be re-assigned dynamically.

What Happens When a Job Is Created

Once the integration chain is active, creating a new job in SmartRecruiter will automatically route the approval to the configured integration user (system user). The job moves into a 'Pending approval' state.

The webhook event job.approval.created fires at this point, triggering your CPI iFlow to take over the approval routing.

Implementing Dynamic Approval Logic in CPI

Your CPI iFlow receives the job.approval.created webhook payload. A Groovy script within the flow reads the relevant job or offer fields, evaluates the business rules, and determines the correct approvers. The implementation follows two API calls to SmartRecruiter.

Step 1: Get the Current Approval (Retrieve baseId)

Call the following endpoint to retrieve the latest approval for the job:

GET https://api.smartrecruiters.com/jobs/{jobId}/approvals/latest

The response includes the approvalRequestId which becomes the baseId for the next call.

Step 2: Create a New Approval with Dynamic Approvers

POST to the Approvals API with the baseId and the dynamically determined approver list:

POST https://api.smartrecruiters.com/approvals-api/v201910/approvals

Request Body:

{
  "baseId": "35a1ef73-4542-4d37-84c2-2b34522327e1",
  "type": "sequential",
  "decisionMode": "any",
  "steps": [
    {
      "approvers": [
        { "id": "6a986436be2958fa852dda78" }   // User A
      ]
    },
    {
      "approvers": [
        { "id": "6a98643697a14f8c43c2a454" }   // User B or C (from Groovy logic)
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Verifying the Dynamic Approval on the SmartRecruiter UI

After the CPI iFlow completes the POST call, refresh the job in SmartRecruiter. The approval panel will now show the dynamically assigned approvers — replacing the original integration user with the correct business approvers as determined by the Groovy logic.

Triggering the Integration via Webhook

The entire flow is event-driven. Configure a SmartRecruiter webhook to fire your CPI iFlow endpoint whenever a job or offer approval is created.

For Job Approvals — subscribe to:

For Offer Approvals — subscribe to:

Extending to Offer Approvals

The exact same pattern applies to offer approvals. The only differences are:

  • GET endpoint to fetch the baseId:
    https://api.smartrecruiters.com/candidates/{id}/jobs/{jobId}/offers/{offerId}/approvals/latest
  • Webhook event: offer.approval.created (instead of job.approval.created).
  • The POST endpoint and request body structure remain identical.

Tip: Reuse the same CPI iFlow for both job and offer approvals by routing on the webhook event type at the message entry point. A single Groovy script can contain all business-rule branches, keyed on the approval subject type ('job' vs 'offer') in the GET response.

Conclusion

The Integration-type approval chain in SAP SmartRecruiter, combined with the Approvals API and SAP CPI, provides a clean, scalable pattern for implementing dynamic, condition-driven approval workflows. Instead of creating dozens of static chains to cover every business scenario, you centralise the routing logic in a single CPI iFlow and let the API handle the assignment at runtime.

This approach is equally applicable to re-triggering rejected approvals — simply listen for the approval-rejected webhook, run your re-routing logic, and POST a fresh approval using the same baseId.

I hope this blog gives you a clear blueprint to get started. Feel free to share your questions or experiences in the comments below!

Thanks

Kunal

entry.title: Aynı Yasal Duyuru, Aynı Değişim… Yoksa Değil mi?
entry.content:
The Question

Open the roadmap. It looks familiar.

Open the H1 2027 Türkiye Payroll roadmap and the first impression is familiar.

Five Legal Changes.
New rules.
New dates.
New payroll work.

The normal question is obvious:

What do we need to change to stay compliant?

For TR00, the established payroll schema, that often means checking what is already supported, updating statutory parameters or enhancing existing logic where required, and keeping the solution aligned with applicable legislation.

Ama…

with TR01, our newer payroll schema, there is another question worth asking.

Can we respond to the legal change without creating the next special case?

And sometimes there is an even more important question: Should we build something new at all?

That changes how I read this roadmap. Not as five identical development commitments, but as five opportunities to make a deliberate product decision.

.......

TR01 is not about redesigning everything every time a new law arrives.

Compliance matters. Her zaman. But the best product response is not always a new payroll function or a new configuration table.

Sometimes we reuse something proven. Sometimes we automate manual administration. Sometimes a statutory scenario helps shape a reusable framework. And sometimes, after listening to the market, we decide that an implementation is not a priority for the current roadmap.

Some enhancements also began with our implementation partners, independently of any particular legal announcement. The legal changes give us a way to test whether those ideas can serve more than one scenario.

Here is how those decisions appear across the five roadmap topics, ordered by their current request delivery targets.

.......

Five Legal Changes, Five Product Decisions

The laws differ. So do the solutions.

Nitelikli Hizmet Merkezi Gelir Vergisi ve Damga Vergisi İstisnası

First, Qualified Service Centers.

The legal change provides an Income Tax and Stamp Tax exemption on qualifying remuneration for eligible personnel, up to a statutory ceiling: three times the gross minimum wage for standard centers and five times for eligible special locations. The amount above the ceiling remains taxable. SGK contributions are not changed by this specific exemption.

For TR00, we have not identified a relevant customer population. Consequently, a TR00 implementation is not planned in the current delivery scope. The legal obligation itself does not disappear for employers to whom it applies.

For TR01, the more valuable direction is not another hard-coded exception for one type of employer.

Instead, we plan a Configurable Statutory Exemption Framework with two distinct approaches: one for exemptions applied to an eligible remuneration base, and another for exemptions on specific additional payments, allowances or benefits.

The design direction includes configurable wage-type eligibility, statutory percentages and ceilings, relevant employee or workplace conditions, and distinct SGK, Income Tax and Stamp Tax treatments. Existing net-to-gross processing should apply those results consistently rather than requiring a separate gross-up engine.

Qualified Service Center is the immediate legal scenario. The ambition is a framework that can support other statutory exemptions when their rules require it.

Yani… not every new exemption deserves its own permanent branch in payroll logic.

.......

Kıdem Tazminatı Tavanı ve Vergiden Müstesna Çocuk Yardımı Tutarları

Next, child allowance.

For the second half of 2026, the Income Tax exemption thresholds for employer-paid child allowances are TRY 787.76 per child up to and including 72 months, and TRY 393.88 for children older than 72 months. Income Tax and SGK exemptions follow different statutory rules.

For TR00, we can build on the existing child-allowance and SGK treatment. The planned work focuses on the age-band Income Tax exemption and on making the allowance easier to maintain: enter the amount per child and eligible child count, then let payroll calculate the total.

For TR01, we can reduce a different manual step.

Instead of requiring HR to enter child counts repeatedly through age-band wage types, the planned enhancement reads IT0021 Family Members, determines eligible children and their age bands, and uses a configurable source for the employer-paid rate.

We are not introducing a separate SGK-to-Income-Tax-base configuration as part of this item. The objective is to automate the data that payroll already needs while preserving the established statutory calculations.

Less duplicate maintenance. More consistent eligibility data.

.......

Uzaktan Çalışma Yönetmeliğinde Değişiklik Yapıldı

Then, remote work.

The September 2026 amendment strengthens contractual requirements for hybrid arrangements, including the distinction between on-site and remote working days and hours. Employers also need to report remote-working days correctly through the applicable e-declaration process.

Here, the lesson is that reuse can be better than reinnovation by invention.

For TR00, reporting of remote-working days is already supported through the existing wage-type classification and e-declaration process, documented in SAP Note 3063529. The immediate task is to validate the customer configuration and the quantity passed to reporting, not to redesign SGK or Income Tax calculations.

For TR01, the planned approach is to reuse that proven pattern: identify the relevant wage type through Evaluation Class 11, carry its remote-working-day quantity in payroll results, and report it using HTRCEDE0.

We are not planning a new generic statutory day-count engine for this legal change. The source and treatment of partial remote-day quantities still need to follow confirmed legal rules and the appropriate existing configuration.

Sometimes the most scalable design decision is simply to avoid building something twice.

.......

SGK Turizm Ücret Desteği Genelgesi Yayımlandı

Tourism Wage Support leads to a different decision.

This temporary measure covers the period from May to December 2026. It is an employer-side support (destek), not an employee SGK or Income Tax exemption. The statutory model uses eligible SGK premium days and a daily amount of TRY 116.67, subject to the applicable employer-premium cap; SGK handles the official offset.

After considering partner feedback and identified customer demand, implementation of Tourism Wage Support is not planned for either TR00 or TR01 in the current scope. That is a product prioritization decision, not a change to employers' legal obligations.

Instead, we are prioritizing a separate TR01 enhancement that partners expect to deliver more everyday value: Recurring Meal Allowance.

Today, maintaining eligible meal days can involve repetitive entries and manual work when a daily rate changes during the month.

The planned TR01 enhancement uses a recurring IT0014 entry, derives eligible days from planned working days and applicable non-working-day information, and prorates the payment when the rate changes. It reuses existing SGK and Income Tax exemption processing rather than inventing new statutory meal rules.

One initiative is deliberately not being built now. Another, independent improvement is moving forward.

That is also a roadmap decision worth explaining.

.......

2027 Asgari Ücret Tespit Komisyonu Kararı ve Gelir Vergisi Tarifesi

And finally, the annual cycle.

At the time of this draft, the official 2027 minimum-wage and Income Tax parameters have not yet been announced. Based on the usual cycle, SAP localization expects the relevant announcements toward the end of December 2026; actual values and effective dates remain subject to the authorities' publications.

For TR00, the established priority is straightforward: update the relevant statutory parameters when confirmed, including the applicable severance ceiling on its own publication and effective-date schedule.

For TR01, the annual update sits alongside a more substantial foundation initiative: bringing Severance/Indemnity calculations into the payroll schema.

The first planned phase covers core statutory severance and notice indemnity calculations, together with a separate monthly severance provision. For that provision, payroll evaluates accumulated service and the applicable full provision at month-end, then calculates the adjustment against the previous month's closing provision balance.

That provision is an accounting calculation, not an employee payment; the precise financial and IFRS/TFRS treatment remains subject to validation.

More advanced termination settlement, off-cycle payment scenarios and annual leave provisioning or payout are possible future extensions, not part of the initial delivery commitment.

The opportunity is to establish a sound payroll foundation now without pretending that every related settlement scenario must be delivered at once.

.......

Beyond Legal Changes — Improving the TR01 Foundation

But not every improvement needs a new law.

During our Türkiye Payroll partner roundtables, some of the most valuable feedback came from everyday implementation experience.

A deduction carried into the wrong payroll split after a company change. A configuration value that consultants must enter manually. An Excel export that removes leading zeros from statutory reporting fields.

Small details?

Perhaps. Until they affect payroll accuracy, require unnecessary workarounds, or interrupt statutory reporting.

That is why, alongside the five Legal Changes, we have also prioritized six TR01 corrections and usability improvements, targeting the end of November 2026.

They address three practical areas:

  • Payroll correctness: Improving carry-forward deduction handling, wage-type processing flexibility, and payroll schema execution.
  • Configuration usability: Making T7TR parameter maintenance easier through search help and IMG integration.
  • Reporting reliability: Preserving leading zeros in E-Declaration Excel exports to avoid invalid reporting files.

None of these requires a new statutory announcement.

They come directly from implementation partners working with TR01 and identifying where the solution can work better.

İşte bu.

Reinnovation is not only about introducing new capabilities. Sometimes it means fixing what gets in the way of using the capabilities we already have.

.......

The Pattern

Put these decisions together and a different pattern emerges.

An established process → reuse and validate it before designing a replacement.

Repeated manual maintenance → derive information from existing employee or working-time data where appropriate.

A recurring statutory scenario → build a configurable framework when it creates genuine reuse.

Limited customer demand → make a transparent decision about what not to prioritize.

Everyday implementation friction → correct the foundation, even without a new law.

Three streams reinforce one another: statutory compliance, reusable product enhancements, and continuous improvement.

They do not always require the same technical response or the same delivery timeline.

.......

The Design Principle

Each legal change invites a design decision — not necessarily new development.

TR01 is not simply TR00 rewritten. And it is not a redesign project hiding behind every legal change.

It is a habit of asking one extra question when change arrives:

What is the simplest sustainable response — reuse, automation, configuration, a focused correction, or a conscious decision to defer?

Not every legal change will produce a reusable capability. Not every partner request will become a committed delivery. And not every proposed improvement needs a new engine.

But every decision should be clear about the customer problem it solves.

.......

Haydi Konuşalım

The best product decisions begin with the right conversations.

If you are implementing TR01, planning a migration, or following the H1 2027 legal changes closely — we have a dedicated space for you.

The Türkiye HCM Localization workspace is where SAP, customers, and partners share implementation experience, ask questions, and shape what comes next.

We have just opened a thread for this roadmap discussion:

Türkiye HCM — H1 2027 Legal Changes: What's Coming & Your Input Matters →

Your edge cases, your implementation experience, your questions — hepsi önemli.

.......

Son Söz

Same legal announcement.

Same need to understand the statutory impact.

But not necessarily the same product change.

TR00 continues to build on its established payroll design. TR01 gives us room to reuse what works, automate what is repetitive, configure what genuinely varies, and improve the foundation based on implementation experience.

These are roadmap intentions and delivery targets, not guarantees that every design detail or planned release date is fixed. Further engineering analysis, statutory guidance and customer feedback may affect the scope.

If you want to follow the progress of the Legal Changes, you can subscribe in SAP Regulatory Change Manager (RCM) for updates.

And I will leave you with a question:

Where in your payroll could a special case become a reusable rule — or where could an existing solution simply be made easier to use?

İşte bu.
